profilePeriod: July 2024–July 2026 premiership; earlier abortion and personal religious context explicitly dated.

sources.title: Final speech as Prime Minister
sources.evidence: Starmer announces resignation and ends his premiership; profile keeps July 2024–July 2026 scope. Official farewell reiterates Ukraine support and shared national identity.

sources.title: English Devolution White Paper
sources.evidence: Widened mayoral authority and funding, housing, transport and skills powers; central government sets framework. Devolution is not sovereign federal states or a right of secession.

sources.title: Serving the country, Labour manifesto
sources.evidence: Pledges removal of hereditary Lords, stronger parliamentary standards, and cooperation with devolved governments; rejects Scottish independence and another referendum.

sources.title: 16 year olds to be given right to vote through election reforms
sources.evidence: Government proposes votes at 16, broader accepted voter identification and easier registration, with foreign-donation safeguards; these are proposals at announcement, not proof of completed implementation.

sources.title: White paper sets out reforms to policing
sources.evidence: Government proposes merging forces, national capabilities, ministerial interventions in failing forces, and a fivefold expansion to 50 live-facial-recognition vans, while retaining local policing.

sources.title: Prime Minister launches clampdown on violent disorder
sources.evidence: Starmer launches National Violent Disorder Programme and greater use of live facial recognition following violent disorder.

sources.title: UK lawmakers back assisted dying bill
sources.evidence: AP independently records Starmer voting for assisted dying for terminally ill adults; government was neutral and colleagues differed. This supports regulated choice, not unrestricted euthanasia.

sources.title: Written question 36759 on cannabis regulation
sources.evidence: Government retains cannabis criminal controls; no general drug liberalisation can be inferred from his human-rights background.

sources.title: PM remarks at Immigration White Paper press conference
sources.evidence: Tighter routes, English requirements and reduced net migration, alongside acknowledgment that migration is part of British history. Integration and common rules are stressed rather than ethnic exclusion.

sources.title: Fewer study and work visas halve net migration
sources.evidence: AP corroborates Starmer tightening work/study visas and English standards while noting earlier Conservative restrictions contributed to the fall. Do not credit all observed reduction to Starmer.

sources.title: PM defence spending announcement
sources.evidence: Defence spending planned at 2.5 percent of GDP by April 2027; domestic defence industrial capacity and new technology supported.

sources.title: UK to buy nuclear-capable F-35 jets
sources.evidence: Starmer announced purchase of 12 F-35A jets and participation in NATO shared nuclear mission, alongside expanded security spending ambitions. These are commitments, not already-delivered aircraft.

sources.title: PM statement recognising Palestine
sources.evidence: Recognises Palestine to advance negotiated two-state peace; condemns Israeli bombardment and humanitarian restrictions and calls for Hamas hostage release and sanctions. Assertive diplomacy with allies is not non-interventionism or conquest.

sources.title: British Steel enters public ownership
sources.evidence: British Steel transferred to public ownership to secure domestic steelmaking; government explicitly retains possible future private investment.

sources.title: NHS and independent-sector agreement
sources.evidence: Government uses independent-sector capacity to reduce NHS waits while preserving publicly funded access; this is neither general privatisation nor exclusion of private providers.

sources.title: Introducing Great British Energy
sources.evidence: New publicly owned energy company intended to accelerate clean energy and domestic energy security.

sources.title: Employment Rights Act receives Royal Assent
sources.evidence: Stronger sick pay, parental leave, dismissal protections and action on exploitative zero-hours contracts; implementation phased over two years, with business and union consultation.

sources.title: International Investment Summit
sources.evidence: Starmer welcomes private and foreign investment and promises to reduce needless regulatory barriers, alongside a state growth strategy.

sources.title: Change, Labour Party Manifesto 2024
sources.evidence: Fiscal discipline and independent Bank of England with 2 percent inflation target; public railway operations and strategic investment; equality commitments. Used as starting-period policy where later evidence does not supersede it.

sources.title: UK concludes trade deal with India
sources.evidence: Free-trade agreement concluded with reductions on most Indian tariff lines affecting UK exports; supports reciprocal liberalisation rather than autarky.

sources.title: Tariffs on non-folding Chinese e-bikes revoked
sources.evidence: Government removes anti-dumping/countervailing tariffs on non-folding e-bikes following economic-interest assessment while preserving measures on folding bikes; sector-specific protection is not universal protectionism.

sources.title: Starmer interview with ITV
sources.evidence: Starmer says he is not personally religious but participates in Jewish family prayers, synagogue visits and traditions, stressing faith matters to his family. This earlier context is explicitly dated.

sources.title: Starmer on Supreme Court gender ruling
sources.evidence: Welcomes biological-sex ruling and single-sex protections while explicitly promising respect and dignity for trans people. Respect for identities is not equivalent to self-identification overriding sex-based law.

sources.title: Government expands nuclear planning
sources.evidence: Supports small modular reactors and wider nuclear siting, removes planning obstacles, and retains safety and environmental standards.

sources.title: AI Opportunities Action Plan government response
sources.evidence: Government backs AI adoption for productivity and public services; technological optimism does not prove support for unregulated human enhancement.

sources.title: Precision breeding plant varieties consultation
sources.evidence: Government continues implementing regulated precision-bred crops under Genetic Technology Act; plant biotechnology must not be conflated with designer human embryos.

sources.title: The Three Pillars of Liberty, Routledge
sources.evidence: Publisher identifies first edition, 1996, and authors Francesca Klug, Keir Starmer and Stuart Weir. Book audits UK political rights, liberties, surveillance, protest, trade unionism and electoral rights.

sources.title: The Three Pillars of Liberty, Berkeley Law catalog
sources.evidence: University library corroborates all three authors, full title, Routledge and 1996 publication.

facts: 2024 devolution programme expands elected mayors’ regional powers.
2026 police reform consolidates national capabilities and ministerial intervention; 2024 manifesto rejects a second Scottish independence referendum.
estrutura.tension: Devolved administration within a preserved union; neither sovereign federalism nor uniform central administration in every service.

facts: 2025 voting reforms extend democratic participation to 16-year-olds and ease registration.
2024 manifesto removes hereditary legislative rights and promotes parliamentary standards.
representacao.tension: Representative parliamentary democracy with legal safeguards; not rule by experts or permanent assembly government, and not unrestricted plebiscites.

facts: 2024 disorder response and 2026 white paper expand police coordination and facial recognition.
Starmer personally voted for terminally ill adults’ assisted dying in June 2025; government retains cannabis controls.
poder.tension: Order and surveillance coexist with legal due process and specific bodily autonomy, not capital punishment or indefinite arbitrary detention.

facts: May 2025 white paper tightens visas and English-language integration requirements.
Starmer acknowledges the national contribution of migration and plural origins.
imigracao.tension: Controlled integration is distinct from ethnically selective entry or suppression of immigrants’ private customs.

facts: February 2025 defence expansion and June nuclear-capable aircraft announcement strengthen NATO deterrence.
September 2025 Palestine recognition advocates negotiated peace.
diplomacia.tension: Strong armed forces and deterrence with diplomacy and lawful action; neither pacifism nor unconditional pre-emptive war.

facts: NATO shared nuclear role, continuing support for Ukraine, and sanctions on Hamas show active external engagement.
Palestine recognition and ceasefire diplomacy support multilateral political settlement.
intervencao.tension: National interest and allied engagement do not imply territorial conquest or rejecting international law whenever inconvenient.

facts: GB Energy and July 2026 British Steel nationalisation provide strategic public ownership.
January 2025 NHS arrangement uses private capacity within public provision.
economia.tension: Mixed ownership, private investment and labour protections; not worker expropriation of all enterprises or prioritising private healthcare.

facts: Employment Rights Act regulates labour relations and expands statutory protections.
Manifesto preserves central-bank independence while investment summit promises regulatory simplification.
controle.tension: Sectoral state planning and worker protection coexist with market pricing, monetary independence and growth-minded deregulation.

facts: May 2025 India trade deal and October 2024 investment summit support international integration.
February 2025 removes tariffs on non-folding Chinese e-bikes but keeps measures on folding bikes; July 2026 steel intervention protects strategic supply.
comercio.tension: Free trade with industrial-security exceptions, not zero tariffs regardless of disruption or national production of everything.

facts: June 2024 ITV interview distinguishes personal nonbelief from valued Jewish family observance.
Constitutional programme supports plural democracy rather than clerical government.
religiao.tension: Secular decision-making and protection for religious communities; atheism does not mean banning faith education, symbols or holidays.

facts: April 2025 supports sex-based protections while insisting on trans dignity.
June 2025 assisted-dying vote supports regulated personal autonomy; manifesto supports equality.
moral.tension: Social equality with limits on gender self-identification and other harm-sensitive regulation, not blanket cultural libertarianism.

facts: January 2025 AI plan and February nuclear expansion put technology at centre of growth.
2025 regulated precision breeding advances crop technology.
tecnologia.tension: Pro-innovation and pro-industry with safety and environmental oversight; no verified commitment to unrestricted designer babies or technological acceleration without limits.

limitations: Profile period preserved exactly from existing research; only its period and source URLs were read. Earlier abortion context is not independently relied upon in this audit; personal-faith evidence is explicitly dated June 2024.
Searches made through 2026-10-01; policy commitments are distinguished from implementation. The profile intentionally ends at July 2026 and does not attribute later governments’ policies to Starmer.
Answers to Brazil-specific examples are analogical applications to equivalent British institutions, not claims of a Starmer position on Brazilian statehood, indigenous jurisdiction or Amazon mining.

No verified personal pronouncements on every question: human enhancement, racial quotas, polyamory and municipal fiscal allocation require cautious principle-based inference. N is reserved for genuine competing principles, not missing evidence.
Primary government/party sources establish policy commitments but not independent measures of success. ITV, AP, parliamentary records and library/publisher sources provide independent cross-checks.
No Brazilian translation of The Three Pillars of Liberty was found in searches of its exact title with Brasil, português and tradução; preserve original title rather than invent a Portuguese one.
